newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends softer at 1,605-1,615 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends softer at 1,605-1,615 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,605-1,615 per dollar, softer from the morning's 1,595-1,615 and Thursday's close at 1,600-1,610, after quiet interbank trade, dealers said.
"Trade was calm and in light volumes. The lev dip by some 10 from Thursday could be considered normal under the current interest rate spread," one dealer said.
The large spread between interest rates on dollar- and lev-denominated deposits allows for a daily lev drop by around 10 per dollar at the current exchange rate levels.
The central bank's main interest rate is now set at 18 percent monthly or 216 percent annually.
The central bank was again seen as the main foreign currency buyer in the market today, dealers said.
The central bank was reported to have actively bought dollars in the market this week, locking in trade between 1,580-1,610 and preventing a sharp lev rise amid the higher dollar supply.

Foreign currency supply from clients has risen amid expectations of a stable or a firmer lev after the interim government and the International Monetary Fund announced a $650 million financial accord on Monday. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
